A small coding or documentation issue can turn into **delayed payments, rework, and lost practice revenue.**

Common denial triggers include:

❌ Documentation that doesn't support the modifier

❌ Incorrect or unsupported modifier usage

❌ NCCI bundling edits

❌ Incorrect telehealth/POS coding

❌ Payer-specific requirements being missed

💡 **The good news:** proactive claim checks, accurate documentation, and proper billing workflows can help reduce avoidable denials.

items.text:
🦶 **Podiatry Billing Is More Complex Than It Looks.**

From **LCDs and NCCI edits to laterality, modifiers, documentation gaps, and payer-specific requirements**, small billing issues can quickly turn into costly claim denials and delayed revenue.

The right **Podiatry Revenue Cycle Management (RCM)** strategy can help your practice:

✅ Prevent avoidable claim denials

✅ Improve coding and documentation accuracy

✅ Strengthen charge capture

✅ Manage A/R and unpaid claims

✅ Improve collections and reimbursement visibility

📈 **Your practice should focus on patient care—not chasing unpaid claims.**

Discover what to look for when comparing podiatry RCM solutions and how specialized expertise can support a healthier revenue cycle.

👉 **Read the full guide:**

[https://www.prcpmd.com/post/compare-podiatry-revenue-cycle-management-for-practices](https://www.prcpmd.com/post/compare-podiatry-revenue-cycle-management-for-practices)

💰 **Where is your medical practice losing revenue?**

A denied claim is often more than a billing problem—it can be a sign of an issue that started earlier in the revenue cycle.

From **patient registration and insurance verification** to **charge capture, coding, claim submission, payment posting, and collections**, every step matters.

That’s why PRCPMD uses the **4-C Revenue Checkpoint:**

🔹 **CAPTURE** — Document services and verify coverage

🔹 **CODE** — Ensure accurate coding

🔹 **CLAIM** — Submit clean, complete claims

🔹 **COLLECT** — Reconcile payments and follow up on balances

The goal isn't just to **fix denials**.

It’s to **fix the process causing them.**
